e: A student injures two faculty members in a school shooting in Aubagne.

Authorities imprison the leader of a sadist Nazi group that forced young women and girls, many of whom were black or Jewish, to perform sexual acts, submit naked pictures, and, in some cases, tortured them.
The US imposes sanctions on Hamas' financing network, which includes two French-based funds.

Following the nationwide spread of high school student protests sparked by complaints about underfunded schools, teacher shortages, and lengthy schedules, Prime Minister Lecornu calls an emergency crisis meeting and orders ministers to cancel official travel.
Pope Leo XIV makes a four-day visit to France.
President Macron announces that the country will send soldiers to protect Saudi Arabia on a Red Sea oil route, as part of an accord with Riyadh.
Vincent Reynouard, a Holocaust denier, receives an eight-month prison sentence.
A passenger train derails in Cléon, injuring 44 people.
A strike is held by staff at the Eiffel Tower in protest over the removal of female employees during a visit by Hindu religious group BAPS.
Four Renoir paintings are stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer.
France sanctions products from Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
A car rams into pedestrians in Caen, killing two people and injuring nine others. The driver is arrested.
France and Saudi Arabia agree to build a $7 billion theme park in the vicinity of Paris.
A tornado hits Pomas, injuring 41 people.
Decision 2026-911: The Constitutional Council rules that the social media ban for minors under 15 years of age violated the rights of minors.

The French Foreign Ministry opens disciplinary proceedings against its ambassador to the Central African Republic, Bruno Foucher, following allegations that he brought around 30 young women to his official residence in Bangui from 2024 to 2026.

A total solar eclipse occurs at the Moon's descending node of the orbit in North America and Europe. The total eclipse passes over the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic Ocean, northeastern Portugal and northern Spain.
A wildfire fire breaks out in Landes, displacing 650 people.
A man wounds three women with two kitchen knives in Paris. Two victims are seriously injured.
Twelve Torah scrolls are stolen from a synagogue in the vicinity of Paris.
The beaches used during the Normandy landings in 1944 are designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Six people are detained in a suspected plot targeting a synagogue in Sarcelles.
A major wildfire breaks out at Fontainebleau forest.
France repatriates 23 antiques to Syria that it had held since the Syrian civil war.
The Paris appeals court allows Marine Le Pen to run for president in 2027 pending the result of an appeal to the Court of Cassation against her conviction for embezzlement of EU funds.
A pilot and ten parachutists are killed when a small plane crashes in Tomblaine.
Burkina Faso breaks off diplomatic relations with France.
A cliff collapses in Biarritz, killing one person and leaving another missing.

France experiences its hottest day on a national scale, with an average temperature of 29.8°C (85.6°F) across the country, beating the previous record of 29.4°C. The highest locally recorded temperature is 44.3°C, in Pissos.
More than 40 deaths from drowning are reported, due to people trying to cool themselves in rivers, canals, and other no-go areas.
The Golfech Nuclear Power Plant is temporarily shut down as water temperatures in the River Garonne exceed the recommended safety limit of 28°C, which is too high to cool the reactors.

US president Donald Trump and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian sign the Islamabad Memorandum to end the 2026 Iran war, with Trump signing the document during dinner with President Macron at the Palace of Versailles.
France prohibits Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entering the country, citing promotion of West Bank annexation and "re-colonization" in Gaza.
Nationwide clashes between police and football fans celebrating Paris St-Germain's victory in the 2026 UEFA Champions League final leave one person dead, 219 injured and 780 arrested.
The initial disappearance of Lyhanna Rameau Bernard, later leading to public outrage and protests.
France bans Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben Gvir from entering the country, citing his “unspeakable” behavior against French and European 2026 Global Sumud Flotilla activists.
France begins refusing temporary residence permits to Russians with humanitarian visas.
France's Monroe finishes 11th at Eurovision 2026 in Austria with their single "Regarde!".
Two migrants die in an attempted crossing of the English Channel to the UK that results in their boat running aground near Neufchatel-Hardelot.
France and the United Kingdom sign a three-year agreement to reduce irregular crossings by migrants in the English Channel.
